Kyiv residents search through the wreckage after Russia’s deadly barrage Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 21/08/2026 - 9:00 GMT+2 Residents of Kyiv’s Solomianskyi district spent Thursday assessing the damage after a Russian overnight barrage of ballistic and cruise missiles and drones tore through a residential area. … More The attack began shortly after midnight on 20 August and lasted for nearly nine hours. In Solomianskyi, the upper floors of a nine-storey apartment block were destroyed, killing at least eight people and leaving others trapped beneath the rubble. Emergency crews rescued 12 residents as they searched the wreckage for survivors. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Rescuers worked through the debris as residents inspected shattered windows, damaged homes and burned vehicles. The strike also damaged nearby civilian infrastructure, including a school and a children’s hospital, according to Ukrainian authorities. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the attack caused extensive damage in three Kyiv districts, with Solomianskyi among the areas hit hardest. The strikes damaged residential buildings and critical infrastructure, while emergency services remained at the scene to clear rubble and secure unsafe structures. The attack highlighted the vulnerability of Kyiv’s civilian areas to Russian ballistic missiles, which are difficult to intercept. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine urgently needed more air-defence interceptors, including Patriot systems capable of engaging some of Russia’s ballistic missiles. Kyiv authorities declared Friday, 21 August, a day of mourning for those killed in the attack. Flags were flown at half-mast and public entertainment events were cancelled across the capital. What we know on day 1,658 Warren Murray with Guardian writers and agencies Mon 7 Sep 2026 21.15 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Ukraine’s prosecutor general, Ruslan Kravchenko, has resigned amid corruption accusations that saw anti-graft officers search his offices at the weekend as part of investigations into illegal call centres. Kravchenko has rejected any allegations against him, calling them “completely unsubstantiated” and denying wrongdoing. The National Anti-Corruption Bureau (Nabu) and Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office (Sapo) announced on Saturday that they had uncovered a money-laundering scheme “led by an official in the prosecutor general’s office” and had conducted raids there. According to investigators, a corrupt network received money to protect call centres that carried out phone scams and “laundered fortunes amounting to millions”. Nabo published images of a safe filled with bundles of dollar bills, saying it uncovered five members behind the scheme, without naming them. A deputy of Kravchenko has been remanded in custody on suspicion of money laundering in connection with the case. Volodymyr Zelenskyy in 2025 faced protests that forced him to reverse efforts to make Nabu and Sapo subordinate to the national prosecutor’s office . According to the Swiss-based Global Initiative Against Transnational Crime (GI-TOC), illegal call centres employ about 60,000 people in Ukraine . On Monday, Kravchenko posted: “I have submitted my resignation as prosecutor general. I do not want the office of prosecutor general to be used as a tool in political confrontation. My position regarding the charges remains unchanged.” Ukraine seeks to seize water company owned by billionaire family of British theatre mogul Read more The new turmoil confronting Zelenskyy, Ukraine’s president, comes after a shootout between Ukraine’s SBU and GUR security and intelligence services . Kyiv is also bedding in new military leadership after Zelenskyy sacked the defence minister and was then forced by protests to sack Ukraine’s military commander-in-chief as well because of feuding between the pair. Russia resumed its attacks on Kyiv , Ukraine’s emergency service said late on Monday. It came after the expiration of a three-day halt in attacks while US envoys visited the capital and Moscow. “Russians attacked Boryspil and Fastiv districts with drones,” the emergency service said. The Kyiv city military administration said an air raid alert was declared in the capital due to the threat of “enemy” drone attack, and urged residents to take shelter. Russia “does not rule out the resumption of the trilateral format ”, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Monday, referring to possible talks involving the Russians, Ukrainians and the US. “But it is too early to say anything about the venue or the exact dates at this stage,” Peskov added. US negotiators told European representatives during talks in Kyiv that Russia was showing a “new willingness” to negotiate over the Ukraine war, the French presidency said on Monday. “The Americans told us that there was a new willingness on the part of Russia to negotiate following the Duma [Russian lower house] elections , and we should prepare for a fresh start to the negotiations,” said an aide to Emmanuel Macron, the French president. Donald Trump’s administration, though, has repeatedly represented Putin’s willingness to meet US representatives and reel off his unaltered maximalist demands as a willingness to negotiate. A Russian ⁠attack damaged ⁠a British ⁠American Tobacco plant ​in the town ⁠of Pryluky in Ukraine’s northern ⁠Chernihiv region with no known injuries, BAT Ukraine’s ⁠press office said. Off-site power at the Zaporizhzhia ⁠nuclear ⁠plant ​in south-eastern Ukraine has been restored via ⁠the Ferosplavna power line, according to Rosatom, the Russian state nuclear corporation ⁠that is illegally in control of the power station. Latvia’s ⁠government plans to impose a 300% tariff on grain arriving ⁠from Russia and ⁠Belarus. Officials in ⁠Latvia and its neighbour Lithuania last week said they considered ending ⁠shipments of Russian grain through their ports ​after Moscow ‌stepped up the ‌transits in response to attacks by Ukraine ‌on its Baltic ports. The UN human rights chief, Volker Türk, said he was “horrified by reports that fully autonomous drones launched by the Russian Federation killed three Ukrainians last month”. Türk called for an urgent ban on such weapons. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Carlson repeatedly suggested to Rees-Mogg that the west was to blame for inviting Russian aggression and said of the prospect Britain could have lost to Hitler: ‘Who cares?’ Composite: Chip Somodevilla, Leon Neal/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Carlson repeatedly suggested to Rees-Mogg that the west was to blame for inviting Russian aggression and said of the prospect Britain could have lost to Hitler: ‘Who cares?’ Composite: Chip Somodevilla, Leon Neal/Getty Images Tucker Carlson Jacob Rees-Mogg accuses Tucker Carlson of ‘verging on defending Hitler’ Former Tory minister defends UK decision to enter war in podcast with US rightwinger and Putin sympathiser Rowena Mason Whitehall editor Sun 4 Oct 2026 06.53 EDT Last modified on Sun 4 Oct 2026 07.44 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The former Tory minister Jacob Rees-Mogg has found himself defending Britain’s decision to fight against Adolf Hitler after inviting the US rightwinger and Vladimir Putin sympathiser Tucker Carlson into his home for an interview. During the encounter, Carlson repeatedly suggested the west was to blame for inviting aggression from Russia and said of the prospect that Britain could have lost to Hitler: “Who cares?” Rees-Mogg, who lost his parliamentary seat in 2024, appears to have agreed to host Carlson’s podcast show after carving out a post-politics career as a commentator. Carlson set up the show after leaving Fox News and losing faith with Donald Trump, largely citing the US president’s willingness to get involved in foreign wars. Carlson has interviewed Putin and taken a sympathetic position towards Russia over Ukraine . In the lengthy debate on foreign policy and global tensjons, the US commentator repeatedly goaded Rees-Mogg over the smallness of the UK armed forces and suggested Russia was more powerful. Rees-Mogg explained that the UK economy was bigger and made the case that Britain and western allies had to support Ukraine and deter Russian aggression. Carlson went on to question why Britain bothered entering the second world war and claimed Germany had a legitimate claim over parts of Poland. Rees-Mogg said: “Otherwise we’d be speaking German.” Carlson replied: “Who cares? There are a lot of people in Britain who can’t speak English. So it would be nice to have at least a European language spoken in your country.” During the interview, Rees-Mogg said he was very surprised that Carlson was “verging on defending Hitler”, adding: “I think this is not really what you want to be doing.” Carlson replied: “Yeah, I guess I’m just a secret Nazi. I’m actually not a secret Nazi … and hardly a public Nazi.” Rees-Mogg responded that he was reassured, before saying that “Germany would have invaded us” if the UK had not gone to war. The interview has raised eyebrows in the US as well as Britain, with Mike Huckabee, the Republican and US ambassador to Israel, posting on X: “When it seemed impossible for Toxic Tucker to descend deeper into the sewer here he goes opining that UK should have let Nazis take over. Forget that Hitler murdered 11 million people? I thought Tucker was against killing? He needs help.
